transcript.text: Thank you, Nadia. During my collateral review this week, I found that $1,500,000 of the $10,000,000 in reported receivables are invoices owed by entities under the borrower's common ownership. Our policy excludes related-party receivables from eligibility, which means the true eligible receivables base is $8,500,000, not $10,000,000. Applying the 80% advance rate, the maximum commitment we can support is $6,800,000 — well below the requested $8,000,000 renewal. I also want to note that an approved renewal at this risk level requires a monthly borrowing-base certificate, and I have not yet entered this finding into the credit system. I'm sharing this now so we can all factor it into our discussion before any terms are issued.

transcript.text: I need to share critical information from a customer call I had this morning. The manufacturer confirmed they must retain at least $2,000,000 of undrawn availability for a seasonal payroll contract. Additionally, the borrower has agreed to pay down exactly $500,000 before the renewal is funded. I recorded this in my client notes, which haven't yet been circulated to credit. This is directly relevant to Victor's findings, because with the corrected eligible receivables base of $8,500,000 and an 80% advance rate, the maximum commitment would be $6,800,000. After the $500,000 paydown, drawn exposure would be $4,500,000, leaving $2,300,000 of undrawn availability under a $6,800,000 facility — which would satisfy the borrower's $2,000,000 minimum undrawn availability requirement.
